title: Three HSE cases, one message: foreseeable risks were not controlled
excerpt: Concrete Connect’s 11 August review of three HSE prosecutions is worth circulating to every TWS and site manager. A timber platform, a rainwater-filled excavation and an unprotected edge to plant movement — all foreseeable, all temporary works territory.
linkedinReady:
Three recent HSE prosecutions. Three different sites. The same lesson.

A timber crash deck with no design. An excavation with makeshift, unsecured timber bridges and no lighting. A dumper into an unprotected excavation after seat belts were disabled.

These are not ‘accidents’. They are failures to plan, manage and monitor construction work — and they sit squarely in temporary works control.

If your inspection only looks at the branded scaffold and ignores the timber platform, the plank over the trench and the edge next to plant, you are inspecting the paperwork, not the risk.

Briefing: https://www.temporaryworksconsulting.com/news.html

#HSE #TemporaryWorks #CDM2015 #ExcavationSafety

body.p: Reporting on 11 August 2026 grouped three HSE prosecutions: the Paxton House timber platform collapse (incident 23 February 2024; fines confirmed June 2026); a labourer drowned after falling into a rainwater-filled foundation excavation at Bovingdon, where unsecured makeshift timber bridges without handrails were used; and a one-tonne dumper overturn into an unprotected excavation after workers had been instructed not to wear seat belts.

body.h: Why this is temporary works, not just ‘H&S’
body.p: Crash decks, excavation access, trench bridging and vehicle-edge protection are temporary works items. They belong on the register, they need a design or a documented standard solution, they need a permit and they need inspection by someone competent for that item. CDM 2015 duties on planning, managing and monitoring construction work are not discharged by a RAMS that nobody supervised.

ul: Add crash decks, debris platforms and ‘temporary boarding’ to the Temporary Works Register — they are structures that carry load.
Ban makeshift excavation bridges. If people must cross, specify a designed or proprietary access with edge protection, bearing and inspection.
Protect excavations against plant and people. An open edge next to a dumper is a temporary works and traffic-management item.
Check that the person signing inspections is actually competent for the item — not merely available.
